title: Black Directors Hold 2.3% of FTSE 100 Board Seats | Across the Water, Ep. 7
lede: Ethnic minority directors now hold 20% of FTSE 100 board seats, a record. Black directors hold 2.3%, and their number fell from 25 to 24 last year. As the 2027 Powerlist names the City of London's first Black chief executive as Britain's most influential Black person, this episode looks inside the Black British boardroom: the board count, the management pipeline, the pay gap and the reporting law still waiting for a bill.
keyPoints: Black directors held 24 of 1,063 FTSE 100 board seats at the end of 2025 (2.3%), down from 25; ethnic minority directors overall held 20% (Parker Review, March 2026).
In the FTSE 250, Black directorships fell from 42 to 37 (2.5% to 2.1%); Black managers were 1.3% of FTSE 100 UK senior management, down from 1.5% (Parker Review).
Census 2021 counted 2.41 million Black people in England and Wales, 4.0% of the population (ONS via GOV.UK).
In 2022, Black employees' median hourly pay was £13.53 vs £14.35 for White employees; UK-born Black employees earned 5.6% less like for like (ONS).
Mandatory ethnicity pay gap reporting for employers with 250+ staff was confirmed on March 25, 2026; the bill has not been introduced and no start date is set.
